subject: english
prompt_en: Listen: 'I wish I were the fruit-seller / Who sings along the lane.' What does the child wish to be?
prompt_hi: Suno — bachcha kya banna chahta hai?
answer: A fruit-seller

subject: english
prompt_en: Why do you think the child wishes to be the gardener 'who digs and never hurries'?
prompt_hi: Bachcha 'never hurries' wala gardener kyun banna chahta hai? Socho, bachche ki apni life kaisi hai.
answer: Because the gardener works calmly outdoors with plants and nobody rushes him, unlike the child who is always hurried

subject: english
prompt_en: Finish: 'A gardener is someone who ___.'
prompt_hi: Pura karo: 'A gardener is someone who ___.' Maali kya karta hai?
answer: grows and looks after plants

subject: english
prompt_en: Which is right: 'the watchman who guards our gate' or 'the watchman which guards our gate'?
prompt_hi: Watchman ek insaan hai — 'who' ya 'which'?
answer: the watchman who guards our gate

subject: english
prompt_en: Find the mistake: 'My mother is teacher in a school.'
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo: 'My mother is teacher in a school.'
answer: My mother is a teacher in a school.

subject: english
prompt_en: Fill in 'a' or 'an': He is ___ electrician.
prompt_hi: 'A' ya 'an' — kaunsa aayega? 'He is ___ electrician.'
answer: an

subject: english
prompt_en: Make your own wish like the poem: 'I wish I were the ___ who ___.'
prompt_hi: Poem jaisa apna wish banao: 'I wish I were the ___ who ___.'
answer: A wish naming a worker and what they do, joined by 'who', e.g. 'I wish I were the pilot who flies above the clouds.'

subject: english
prompt_en: Listen: 'Or the watchman with his lantern / Who keeps away our worries.' What does this line mean?
prompt_hi: 'Keeps away our worries' — watchman hamari worries kaise door karta hai?
answer: He guards us at night, so we can sleep without fear

subject: english
prompt_en: Ravi says, 'A sweeper's job is small.' Do you agree? Give a reason.
prompt_hi: Ravi kehta hai safai ka kaam chhota hai. Kya tum agree karte ho? Reason do.
answer: No; every job matters. Without sweepers our streets would be dirty and people could fall sick

subject: english
prompt_en: 'Maali' in Hindi. What is it in English? And 'chowkidar'?
prompt_hi: 'Maali' aur 'chowkidar' ko English mein kya kehte hain?
answer: Gardener; watchman

subject: english
prompt_en: Explain to your younger brother what the poem is about and what it teaches.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ko samjhao — poem kis baare mein hai aur kya sikhati hai.
answer: A child wishes to be different workers (a fruit-seller, a gardener, a watchman) because each job has something he loves; it teaches that every kind of work deserves respect

subject: english
prompt_en: Put the steps in order: (a) The coil is cut into rings. (b) Glass is melted in a hot furnace. (c) The rings are joined over a flame. (d) The bangles are painted.
prompt_hi: Choodi banne ke steps ko order mein lagao.
answer: b, a, c, d

subject: english
prompt_en: Which is right: 'Bangles are made in Firozabad' or 'Bangles are make in Firozabad'?
prompt_hi: Kaunsa sahi — 'are made' ya 'are make'?
answer: Bangles are made in Firozabad

subject: english
prompt_en: Fill in: The bangles are ___ (paint) with gold lines.
prompt_hi: 'Paint' ka sahi form lagao: The bangles are ___ with gold lines.
answer: painted

subject: english
prompt_en: Find the mistake: 'These bangles are make by hand.'
prompt_hi: Galti dhoondo: 'These bangles are make by hand.'
answer: These bangles are made by hand.

subject: english
prompt_en: Noor loves the clink of bangles at festivals, but she knows how hot and hard the work is. How do you think she feels about her family's work?
prompt_hi: Noor ko choodiyan pasand hain, par usse pata hai kaam garam aur mushkil hai. Woh apni family ke kaam ke baare mein kaisa feel karti hogi?
answer: Proud of her family's skill, and also caring or worried because the work is hot and hard

subject: english
prompt_en: Papa says, 'Every bangle is made by many hands.' What does he mean?
prompt_hi: 'Every bangle is made by many hands' — Papa kya keh rahe hain?
answer: Many workers each do one step (melting, shaping, cutting, joining, painting) to make one bangle

subject: english
prompt_en: Which word tells the sound bangles make: 'clink' or 'glow'?
prompt_hi: Choodiyon ki awaaz ke liye kaunsa word hai — 'clink' ya 'glow'?
answer: clink

subject: english
prompt_en: Find the spelling mistake: 'Dadi wears red bangels.'
prompt_hi: Spelling ki galti dhoondo: 'Dadi wears red bangels.'
answer: bangels should be bangles

subject: english
prompt_en: 'Choodiyan' in Hindi. What is it in English? And 'bhatti'?
prompt_hi: 'Choodiyan' aur 'bhatti' ko English mein kya kehte hain?
answer: Bangles; furnace

subject: english
prompt_en: A glass bangle is dropped on a stone floor. What will probably happen, and why?
prompt_hi: Glass ki choodi patthar ke farsh par gir jaaye toh kya hoga? Kyun?
answer: It will probably break, because glass is fragile and breaks easily

subject: english
prompt_en: Describe how rotis are made at home in three steps, using 'first', 'then' and 'finally'.
prompt_hi: Ghar mein roti kaise banti hai? 3 steps mein batao — first, then, finally.
answer: Three steps in order with sequence words, e.g. 'First the dough is made. Then it is rolled flat. Finally it is cooked on the tawa.'

subject: english
prompt_en: Explain to a friend why we should value glass bangles, using what you know about how they are made.
prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao — glass ki choodiyon ki keemat kyun karni chahiye? Banane ke tareeke ke baare mein batao.
answer: Each bangle goes through many steps (melting in a hot furnace, shaping, cutting, joining, painting) done by many skilled workers in hard, hot conditions, so we should handle bangles with care and respect the workers

subject: evs
prompt_en: Where is most of Earth's water found: in rivers, in seas and oceans, or in ponds and lakes?
prompt_hi: Earth ka sabse zyada paani kahaan hai: nadiyon mein, samudra aur mahasagar mein, ya taalab aur jheelon mein?
answer: In the seas and oceans; about 97 out of every 100 parts of Earth's water is salty sea water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Take a steel glass of ice-cold water from the fridge and wipe its outside dry. Predict first: after five minutes, will the outside stay dry or get wet? If it gets wet, where will that water come from?
prompt_hi: Fridge se barf jaise thande paani ka steel glass nikalo aur bahar se poochh ke sukha kar do. Pehle guess karo: paanch minute baad glass bahar se sukha rahega ya geela ho jayega? Agar geela hua, toh woh paani kahaan se aayega?
answer: The outside gets covered with tiny drops. They come from invisible water vapour in the air that turns back into liquid when it touches the cold glass (condensation); the water inside does not leak out.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Two equally wet handkerchiefs: one spread open in the sun, one folded up in a shady corner. Predict which one dries first, and where its water goes.
prompt_hi: Do barabar geele rumaal: ek dhoop mein khol ke phailaya, ek chhaanv wale kone mein tah karke rakha. Guess karo kaunsa pehle sookhega, aur uska paani kahaan jayega?
answer: The one spread open in the sun dries first; warmth and a bigger open surface make the water evaporate faster. The water goes into the air as invisible water vapour; it is not destroyed.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Stir two spoons of salt into half a cup of water, pour it into a plate and leave it in the sun for two or three days. Predict: what will be left on the plate?
prompt_hi: Aadhe cup paani mein do chammach namak ghol do, plate mein daal ke do-teen din dhoop mein rakh do. Guess karo: plate mein kya bachega?
answer: The water evaporates and white salt is left behind on the plate. This is how salt is made from sea water in salt pans, for example in Gujarat.

subject: evs
prompt_en: There is so much water on Earth, yet many towns in India run short of drinking water every summer. Why?
prompt_hi: Earth pe itna saara paani hai, phir bhi har garmi mein India ke kai shehron mein peene ka paani kam pad jaata hai. Aisa kyon?
answer: Most of Earth's water is salty sea water, and most of the fresh water is frozen ice or deep under the ground; only a tiny part is in rivers, lakes and wells we can reach, and very many people share it.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Rain clouds get much of their water from the salty sea. So why is rain water not salty?
prompt_hi: Baarish ke baadal apna kaafi paani khaare samudra se lete hain. Phir baarish ka paani khaara kyon nahi hota?
answer: When sea water evaporates, only the water rises as vapour; the salt stays behind in the sea. So clouds and rain are fresh water.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Compare the water in a glacier high in the Himalayas with the water in the Arabian Sea. How are they different, and which one is fresh water?
prompt_hi: Himalaya ke glacier ke paani aur Arabian Sea ke paani ki tulna karo. Dono mein kya farak hai, aur kaunsa meetha (fresh) paani hai?
answer: Glacier water is solid ice and fresh, not salty; sea water is liquid and salty. Glacier ice melts slowly and feeds rivers like the Ganga.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Where does the water in your home's tap or handpump come from? Trace it back as far as you can.
prompt_hi: Tumhare ghar ke nal ya handpump ka paani kahaan se aata hai? Jitna peeche tak jaa sako, utna batao.
answer: From fresh water: a river, lake or dam reservoir through pipes and a tank, or from water under the ground through a borewell, well or handpump. All of it first came from rain or melting snow.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Chennai is right next to the sea, yet it sometimes faces water shortage. The city has built big plants that remove salt from sea water. Why can't every city just do this instead of saving water?
prompt_hi: Chennai bilkul samudra ke paas hai, phir bhi wahaan kabhi-kabhi paani ki kami hoti hai. Shehar ne bade plant banaye hain jo samudra ke paani se namak nikaalte hain. Har shehar bas yahi kyon nahi kar leta, paani bachane ki jagah?
answer: Removing salt from sea water needs big machines and a lot of electricity, so it is costly; it cannot replace saving water and keeping rivers, lakes and ground water clean.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Draw 100 small boxes to stand for all of Earth's water. Colour how many are salty sea water, how many are frozen ice, and how many are fresh water we can use. Then tell me what your drawing shows.
prompt_hi: 100 chhote dabbe banao jo Earth ke saare paani ko dikhayein. Rang bharo: kitne dabbe khaara samudra, kitne jami hui barf, aur kitne woh meetha paani jo hum use kar sakte hain. Phir batao tumhari drawing kya dikhati hai.
answer: About 97 boxes for salty sea water, about 2 boxes for ice and glaciers, and less than 1 box shared by ground water, rivers and lakes; usable fresh water is a tiny part.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Pinky says: 'When a puddle dries in the sun, the water is finished forever. The sun destroys it.' What is wrong with Pinky's idea?
prompt_hi: Pinky kehti hai: 'Jab dhoop mein gaddhe ka paani sookh jaata hai, toh paani hamesha ke liye khatam ho jaata hai. Suraj use mita deta hai.' Pinky ki baat mein galti kya hai?
answer: The water is not destroyed. It evaporates into the air as invisible water vapour, which later cools into clouds and comes back down as rain.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Your little cousin thinks steam, ice and rain are three totally different things. Explain to him how they are all water, and why we must not waste fresh water.
prompt_hi: Tumhara chhota cousin sochta hai ki bhaap, barf aur baarish 3 bilkul alag cheezein hain. Use samjhao ki ye sab paani hi hain, aur hume meetha paani barbaad kyon nahi karna chahiye.
answer: Ice (solid), liquid water and water vapour (gas) are the same water in different forms; cooling and warming change the form. Very little of Earth's water is fresh and usable, so saving it matters.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Quick one from last time: out of every 100 buckets of Earth's water, about how many are salty?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se ek jaldi wala sawaal: Earth ke har 100 baalti paani mein se lagbhag kitni baaltiyaan khaari hain?
answer: About 97.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Name three ways your body loses water in a day.
prompt_hi: 3 tareeke batao jinse tumhare shareer se din bhar mein paani nikalta hai.
answer: Sweating, breathing out water vapour, and passing urine (tears too).

subject: evs
prompt_en: Put a white flower (like a white rose or guldaudi) or a leafy stem in a glass of water with a few drops of food colour. Ask an adult to cut the stem fresh. Predict: what will you see on the petals or leaves after a day?
prompt_hi: Ek safed phool (jaise safed gulab ya guldaudi) ya patton wali tehni ko paani ke glass mein rakho jismein khaane ka rang ki kuch boondein daali hon. Tehni kisi bade se taaza katwa lo. Guess karo: ek din baad pankhudiyon ya pattiyon pe kya dikhega?
answer: The colour shows up in the petals or in the veins of the leaves, because water travels up the stem from the bottom to the top.

subject: evs
prompt_en: In the morning, tie a clear plastic bag around one leafy branch of a plant standing in the sun (only the branch, not the whole plant). Predict: what will you see inside the bag by evening?
prompt_hi: Subah dhoop mein khade paudhe ki ek patton wali daal pe saaf plastic ki thaili baandh do (sirf daal pe, poore paudhe pe nahi). Guess karo: shaam tak thaili ke andar kya dikhega?
answer: Water drops and mist inside the bag. The leaves give out water vapour through tiny openings, and it turns into drops on the bag; this water came up from the roots.

subject: evs
prompt_en: Two drooping potted plants: for one you spray water only on the leaves; for the other you pour water into the soil. Predict which one will stand up straight first.
prompt_hi: Do murjhaye hue gamle ke paudhe: ek ki sirf pattiyon pe paani chhidko, doosre ki mitti mein paani daalo. Guess karo kaunsa paudha pehle seedha khada hoga.
answer: The one watered in the soil, because its roots take up the water and send it up the stem to the leaves.
